title: How is a customer roll fee waived as goodwill on a Container Bookings booking?
content:
## When this applies
This entry covers the Container Bookings product line. At the verified customer's request the desk may waive a customer roll fee entry of a booking as goodwill. The waiver cancels the whole fee entry, never part of it, and is written as one waiver entry for the entry's full amount, with the fee entry as its reference.

## Business effect of the waiver
The waiver adds one goodwill waiver entry, dated today, to the booking's charge history, pointing at the fee entry it cancels, and lowers the booking's outstanding charges by exactly the amount passed in. The cancelled fee entry itself stays in the history unchanged, and the booking's sailing, containers and status are not touched.

## How it is invoked
The waiver is written with **waive_customer_roll_fee_66cbaf18**, an internal tool that must first be unlocked (unlock) and then called (call) by the agent. The tool books exactly the amount passed in; it does not compute an amount and does not check any business condition.

## Parameters
| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| booking_id | the booking reference number of the booking whose fee is waived, as returned by the booking lookup for the verified customer | identifier |
| customer_id | the customer reference number of the booking party, as returned by the customer profile lookup | identifier |
| reference_event_id | the reference number of the customer roll fee entry being waived, as shown in the booking's charge history or in the receipt of the charge that booked it | identifier |
| waiver_usd | the amount waived, in USD | a positive decimal amount with 2 decimal places; a value given with more digits is rounded half-to-even to 2 decimal places when booked |

## Return
The tool returns a text rendering of a dictionary describing the booked waiver: booking_event_id (reference of the new waiver entry), booking_id (the booking concerned), charge_code (always waiver), reference_event_id (the fee entry cancelled), amount_usd (the amount waived, USD with 2 decimal places), event_date (YYYY-MM-DD, the booking date of the waiver) and charges_due_usd (the booking's outstanding charges after the waiver, USD with 2 decimal places). A returned booking_event_id means the waiver is on the account. The entry carries the booking's equipment type and records no container count.

## Points of judgement
**Does the waiver delete the fee entry?** No. The fee entry stays in the history; the waiver entry sits next to it and offsets it in full.
